analysis:
## The 50-DMA reclaim

For two weeks BTC has been trapped below its 50-day moving average — every bounce failing at the level, every session another reminder of the downtrend. Today that changed. BTC rallied +3.34% to $63,565, reclaiming the 50-DMA (~$61,900) cleanly and pushing within $90 of the 200-DMA (~$63,654). That is the first technically meaningful bullish development since early June.

The catalyst was shared with equities: [Iran's morning announcement of a formal Strait of Hormuz closure](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-june-11-2026) sent BTC down to $61,099 at the open. Then Trump administration and Iranian officials signaled a deal was close — and the full risk-on reversal followed. Nasdaq +2.54%, BTC +3.34%, WTI still elevated at $93.44 with geopolitical premium intact.

## Technical analysis

The trend read: **shifting from corrective to potentially resuming the bull trend** — confirmation pending a close above the 200-DMA.

**Volume:** Crypto.com exchange volume for June 11 was ~$255M, slightly below the ~$317M of June 10 and ~$312M of June 9. The 50-DMA reclaim came on declining volume, which is a mild concern — but in a geopolitical-news-driven reversal session, volume naturally concentrates at the extremes (morning Hormuz dip, afternoon recovery), and total market 24h volume is estimated ~$28B.

**Momentum:** RSI was at ~35 (oversold) entering today. With the +3.34% move, it is recovering toward neutral. MACD is still negative but narrowing. Recovery from oversold on a clean positioning slate (perp funding near zero, [Fear & Greed at 14](https://milkroad.com/fear-greed/)) is the classic setup that precedes meaningful bounces.

**★ Strongest support: $61,099–$61,510.** This range held as the intraday low three times this week (June 9, 10, 11 — $61,099 being today's Hormuz-panic low). It represents a significant volume shelf with confirmed buyers. The 50-DMA is now embedded in this zone as the first technical backstop. A daily close below $61,099 would signal the bounce has failed.

**★ Strongest resistance: $63,654–$63,935.** The 200-DMA (~$63,654) sits at the lower end; today's intraday high was $63,935. This band has repelled every rally attempt since early June. A confirmed daily close *above* $63,935 — ideally on expanding volume — would be the first genuine bull signal: BTC above both its 50- and 200-DMA for the first time in weeks, with the 200-DMA potentially flipping to support.

**The $65,000 gate.** At $63,565, BTC is 2.3% away from the FOMC re-risk trigger. If FOMC on June 17 delivers anything short of an outright rate-hike signal, the pre-positioning squeeze toward $65K and above would be rapid and sharp — given Fear & Greed at 14 and [11 straight sessions of ETF outflows](https://bitcoinfoundation.org/news/crypto-etfs-news/etf-outflows-june-2/), there are few sellers between here and $67K once $65K clears. That squeeze is the trade to position for.

## The risk that won't resolve overnight

Iran's Hormuz closure is not a one-day headline. WTI at $93.44 sustains headline CPI above 4%, which keeps the Warsh Fed frozen. Even if deal signals are real, the structural oil-supply disruption takes weeks to unwind. The bull case requires FOMC to hold without a hike signal — probable on this data, but not certain. The stop at $59,227 is not optional.
